$comment: Every COUNTED claim the canon makes, and how to check it. Enforced by
tools/check_doc_claims.py::counted_claim_failures.
check_doc_claims.py's own docstring asked for this file by name: it said the gate 'does not check
the front page's COUNTED claims ... which need a declaration mapping each to the command that
prints it', and left the drift to be caught by hand in README_CLAIM_HISTORY.md section 5. It WAS
caught by hand, four audit rounds running, which is how long a by-hand rule lasts.
TWO KINDS OF CLAIM, and the difference is the point.
derive != null  -- countable from the tree in milliseconds with no dependencies, so the gate
recomputes it every run and a wrong number is RED. There is no excuse for
one of these going stale.
derive == null  -- needs a suite to RUN, or a network call, which a gate must not do. These
cannot be verified here, so what is enforced instead is their PROVENANCE: an
environment, a date and a head.
AND THE RULE THAT ACTUALLY CATCHES DRIFT: every file in `cited_in` must CONTAIN the current value
and must NOT contain any value in `superseded`. A declaration that agrees with the tree while the
document beside it still says the old number would be a third copy, not a check on the other two.
The claim-history ledger is deliberately NOT in any `cited_in` list: old numbers belong there.
WHY THE SKIP COUNTS ARE NOT A CLAIM. Measured at one head (2026-09-20) in three environments:
2243 tests RAN in all three, and 14 / 82 / 97 were skipped on the ubuntu runner, the Windows
runner and the Builder's Windows box. A skip count is not a property of the code, and not even of
the PLATFORM -- it is a property of the environment, and three canonical files stated one number
as fact with no environment named. The count is the invariant; the skips are recorded below as
measurements, not asserted in prose.
Stdlib only, deliberately: `check_doc_claims` is 'stdlib plus git, offline' and the CI job that
runs it installs nothing. The ci.yml job count therefore uses a SCOPED scan of that block rather
than a YAML parse -- the whole-file 2-space-indent regex the README warns about answers 23,
because `push:` and `pull_request:` sit at that indent under `on:`.
WHY `superseded` APPEARS ON ONLY TWO CLAIMS. It is an absence rule, and absence of a SMALL number
from a long document is not checkable: measured before shipping this, `40` appears in README.md,
`39` in PROJECT_STATE.md and `21`/`23` in all three, none of them as a claim about gates or jobs.
So the rule is used only where the value is distinctive enough for its presence to mean something
-- four-digit suite counts -- and never on a claim the gate can simply recompute, where the
recomputation is the stronger signal anyway.
WHY THE HEADS NAME A COMMIT ON `main` AND NOT THE BRANCH THE MEASUREMENT RAN ON. These five first
said `9659281`, the branch commit the suites actually ran on. CI refused it: this repository
SQUASH-merges and deletes the branch, so that commit exists in the Builder's clone and nowhere
else -- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 9659281 origin/main` is false. The squash commit `9cc4d2c`
has a BYTE-IDENTICAL tree (99130a751fc1e6a0277184efb595708b7814aae8, checked both ways), so the
measurement holds there and that head is durable. The check below now requires reachability from
`main` rather than mere existence, because 'resolves in my clone' is exactly the asymmetry that
turned this file red on its first CI run.
THE HEADS NAME DIFFERENT COMMITS ON PURPOSE. `engine_tests` moved 2243 -> 2259 in #279, and that
pull request could not declare it: a value measured on a branch cannot cite a landed head, because
the head does not exist until it merges. So the three-environment comparison stays labelled with
the head it was actually measured at (9cc4d2c) and the new count carries its own. Restating the
ubuntu and windows figures at d09661c would be inventing two measurements nobody took.

frontend_test_files.command: cd apps/desktop && npm test   (the 'Test Files' line)

ci_jobs.command: the `jobs` KEY of .github/workflows/ci.yml, parsed as YAML

engine_tests.command: BRO_ENV=ci python -m unittest discover -s engine/tests -t engine/tests -q

bridge_tests.command: BRO_ENV=ci python -m unittest discover -s bridge/tests -t bridge/tests -q

frontend_tests.command: cd apps/desktop && npm ci && npm test
frontend_tests.note: jsdom, so unlike the engine suite this figure does not vary by host.

a11y_tests.command: cd apps/desktop && npm ci && npm run test:a11y

rust_workspace_crates.note: Derivable in principle, but only by parsing TOML or shelling out to cargo, and this gate is stdlib-plus-git with no cargo on its runner.
